subject: Consumption smoothing addendum and phased usage buffer - legal review needed
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightwave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Elena Ross <elena.ross@brightwave.ai>, procurement@brightwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Consumption smoothing addendum proposal

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks again for the onboarding call yesterday. As discussed, our usage for Q3 is expected to spike and then settle down; procurement asked whether we can add a short addendum that "smooths" consumption for billing purposes to avoid an outsized invoice in July while we complete the ramp.

I attached a draft addendum (BrightWave-Consumption-Smoothing-Addendum_v1.docx) that proposes:
- a 3-month consumption buffer where billed committed tokens are averaged across the quarter for invoice purposes, with a true-up at quarter end;
- a temporary credit mechanic (up to 10% of committed units) if actual consumption in month 1 exceeds committed capacity but the quarter average remains < committed;
- a small SOW exhibit tweak so Exhibit 2 reflects the phased ramp schedule.

We can sign an addendum and still keep the MSA intact; procurement suggested a 2-week turnaround if legal can confirm wording. Can you confirm who on Redwood legal should look at this and whether the proposed credit language is acceptable?

Attachments: BrightWave-Consumption-Smoothing-Addendum_v1.docx

Best,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightWave

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightwave.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Elena Ross <elena.ross@brightwave.ai>, procurement@brightwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consumption smoothing addendum proposal

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear draft.

Karthik: I routed the doc to legal and procurement ops. Hannah, can you confirm the credit cap math below and whether finance needs a PO amendment or just an amended order form? We expect the addendum to be an Exhibit-level addition referencing MSA Section 3.2 (billing & invoicing) with a short SOW Exhibit 2 update.

Quick asks for legal:
- Is the language around the 3-month averaging sufficient or should we specify lookback windows / rounding conventions?
- For the temporary credit mechanic, legal: please advise if we need to add a reciprocal obligation for BrightWave to provide monthly usage reports within X days.

Priya: target for us is to get redlines back by Tuesday (6/16) so we can get this into DocuSign the following week. I attached the redlines PDF after my quick markup.

Attachments: redlines_brightwave_2026_06_12.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightwave.ai>, Elena Ross <elena.ross@brightwave.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consumption smoothing addendum proposal

Marissa — thanks for the quick loop.

Hannah: high level from GTM — BrightWave wants predictable spend while ramping; we can accommodate within the existing pricing band if we treat the buffer as an invoicing mechanism, not as a permanent change to committed units. If finance signs off, we should do a 3-month average true-up and keep the committed SKU intact.

Two practical points for legal to consider in redlines:
1) Define the measurement period explicitly (e.g., "monthly usage recorded UTC, aggregated into calendar months; quarterly averaging for billing shall be calculated as the arithmetic mean of the three calendar months comprising the quarter").
2) Add an operational clause: BrightWave shall provide usage exports by the 5th business day after month close or credits are forfeited.

If legal prefers, we can add a short acceptance/termination trigger in the addendum that allows Redwood to opt out if aggregation materially increases operational risk. Not ideal for BrightWave but protects us.

Priya: if you can confirm whether procurement needs a revised PO number for the addendum that speeds signature, call it out.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightwave.ai>, procurement@brightwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-13T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consumption smoothing addendum proposal - numbers and invoice flow

Quick calc for transparency: BrightWave committed 12M units Q3; forecast month-by-month (June, July, August) 2M / 7M / 3M. If we do a 3-month averaging for billing, billed committed tokens = avg(2,7,3)=4M per month for the quarter (12M total), so the invoice spike is flattened. The proposed credit (up to 10% of committed units) would only apply within a month where actual > billed average and the quarter still nets under committed; that’s a relatively small potential credit exposure (worst-case ~1.2M units across quarter).

From finance/process POV:
- We prefer not to change the order form SKU or committed units; addendum references existing order form ID and MSA.
- For invoicing: add a "quarterly true-up" line item that will appear on the last month invoice of the quarter.
- PO changes: procurement noted they'd rather issue a PO amendment referencing the addendum number rather than a whole new PO. So if legal adds an addendum number field, procurement can reference it.

For legal phrasing suggestions: see Karthik's proposed language on measurement and the operational clause. Also suggest a short procedural workflow: monthly usage exports -> interim invoices reflect smoothed billing -> quarter true-up invoice shows net settlement.

Hannah Schmitt
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodai.com>, Legal Team <legal@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightwave.ai>, Elena Ross <elena.ross@brightwave.ai>, procurement@brightwave.ai
Date: 2026-06-14T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Consumption smoothing addendum proposal - legal kickoff and target timeline

Team —

Summarizing next steps and asks so legal has one email thread:
1) Legal: please review the attached redlines (redlines_brightwave_2026_06_12.pdf) and confirm whether the measurement language below is acceptable or needs edits: 
   - "Monthly usage will be recorded in UTC and aggregated into calendar months. Billing for the quarter will be calculated as the arithmetic mean of the three calendar months comprising the quarter."
2) Legal: advise if the credit mechanic needs an explicit expiration or reporting reciprocity (we propose BrightWave must deliver usage exports by the 5th business day after month close).
3) Legal / Contracts: please produce a clean addendum (1–2 pages) referencing MSA Section 3.2 and Order Form #BW-3891, and add an Addendum ID field that procurement can reference in a PO amendment. Target: first draft redlines by EOD Tuesday (6/16).
4) Finance/RevOps (Hannah): confirm the "quarterly true-up" invoice line item label you'd prefer so procurement/ops can map it.
5) Karthik / Marissa: after legal redlines we will send to BrightWave for a 48-hour review window; plan to route to DocuSign the week of 6/22.

Priya / Elena: thanks for the draft — we should be able to meet your cadence if legal can turn in the redlines by 6/16. If procurement needs the PO amendment number sooner, let us know.

Quoted for context: Priya's original request and attached draft.

Attachments: redlines_brightwave_2026_06_12.pdf, BrightWave-Consumption-Smoothing-Addendum_v1.docx
